Q1: Tetracycline hydrochloride exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for Carcinogenicity, Mutagenicity, or Reproductive Toxicity (CMR), environmental concerns (ENV), oral exposure (ORL), and organ/systemic effects (OGN). It also shows expanded potential hazards (Tier 2) for inhalation (IHL) and dermal/eye (SKN) exposures, based on current scientific data. However, there is insufficient information to confidently assess its endocrine disruption hazards (EDC), placing it in Tier 4 for this category.
Q2: Tetracycline hydrochloride is listed on California's Proposition 65, which identifies chemicals known to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. This listing requires businesses to inform Californians about potential exposures to the substance.
Q3: This chemical is very well characterized, supported by an extensive body of scientific literature with 7,184 references, far exceeding the median for similar compounds. Its precise molecular formula and clear substance classification indicate a well-defined structure, and it is not classified as a poorly defined UVCB material. Furthermore, only one out of seven hazard categories (Endocrine Disruption) is considered data deficient, reinforcing its overall comprehensive hazard profile.
